name: table
description: A semantic data table. Purely presentational — renders HTML table elements. Three component sets: table-head (header cells), table-cell (47 content types), and _table-row (rows with state). No built-in sorting or filtering — use TanStack Table for that.

table-head.purpose: Column header cell — label + optional sort indicator (Sort=None/Asc/Desc).

table-cell.purpose: Data cell — 25 content Types across Default and Compact sizes.

intent.None: Column is not sortable or sort is inactive — label only.
intent.Asc: Column sorted ascending — label + upward chevron.
intent.Desc: Column sorted descending — label + downward chevron.

table-cell Type.notes: Avatar-Text, Input, and Select are Default size only.

_table-row State.notes: Header has Default only; Footer has Default and Hover; Regular has all three.

tableContainer.note: ALWAYS use radius/base — canonical table radius. Never use radius/lg, radius/md, or hardcoded values.

composition.assembly: The full table is a FRAME (not a component) containing _table-row instances. No 'table' component set exists.
composition.rowContents: _table-row is H AUTO-LAYOUT containing table-cell or table-head instances.
composition.containerRadiusRule: Outer FRAME radius must be radius/base. Individual rows have no radius — corner clipping is handled by the container's overflow:hidden.
composition.slotTypes: Slot-1 (1 SLOT, 56px), Slot-2 (2 SLOTs, 84px), Slot-3 (3 SLOTs, 112px), Slot-4 (4 SLOTs, 140px). Buttons in slot cells: always Size=Small.

behavior.sortingNotes: Sort=Asc/Desc are visual states only — implement sorting in TanStack Table or parent state.
behavior.rowSelectionNotes: State=Selected is visual only — selection logic lives in parent state.
behavior.hoverNotes: State=Hover is Figma-only. In code use CSS :hover pseudo-class.
behavior.inlineEditing: Type=Input renders <input> inside <td>; Type=Select renders <select> inside <td>.
behavior.dragReorder: Type=Drag shows drag handle — wire to dnd-kit or similar for actual reordering.

accessibility.tableRole: native <table> landmark — no additional role needed
accessibility.rowHeaders: <th scope='row'> on first cell when it's a meaningful row identifier
keyboard: Sort header Enter to toggle sort direction
Drag: Space to pick up, Arrow keys to move

constraints: Always use radius/base on the outer table container FRAME — never radius/lg, radius/md, or hardcoded values.
Never apply radius to individual _table-row instances — the container handles corner clipping.
Always use Type=Header row for column headers — never style a Regular row to look like a header.
Always use Type=Footer for totals/summaries — never use a Regular row.
Type=Input and Type=Select are Default size only — never use in Compact tables.
Button cells in Slot types must use Size=Small.
Type=Button is for one row action; use Type=Action-dropdown for two or more.

useCases: Invoice or transaction lists where each row has a fixed set of columns (date, amount, status, actions)
User or member management panels with sortable columns and row-level actions
Product inventory tables with filtering, inline editing, and status badges per row
Analytics dashboards displaying metric breakdowns by dimension (channel, campaign, cohort)
Order management views combining avatar, status badge, trend indicators, and action dropdowns
Admin data grids that require drag-to-reorder rows and column sorting

table-head Sort=None.whenToUse: Column is informational and not sortable

table-cell Type=Badge.whenToUse: Categorical status that needs a visual chip

table-cell Type=Trend-Up.whenToUse: Percentage change with positive semantic color

_table-row Size=Default.whenToUse: Standard data density — readable without strain

_table-row Size=Compact.whenToUse: High data density needed — secondary or nested panels

comparedTo.situation: Many rows of uniform structured data with column headers and sorting
A vertical list of richer entries with image, multi-line text, and action button
A single self-contained block of information (metric, profile, settings)
A small set of non-tabular key-value pairs within a panel

notes: Table is assembled as a FRAME — there is no single <Table> wrapper component in Figma. In code, use shadcn Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell.

darkMode.notes: No known dark mode differences — all tokens are semantic and mode-aware.
